title: Microglial NCAM1 attenuates ischemic brain injury by inhibiting NF-kappaB-driven neuroinflammation through IkappaBalpha stabilization.
authors: Yu, Zongdong; Yu, Luli; Lu, Wei; Chen, Peng; Yan, Huan; Jiang, Yong'an
one_liner_zh: 该文研究微胶质细胞NCAM1通过稳定IkappaBalpha抑制NF-kappaB神经炎症减轻脑缺血损伤，涉及分子对接筛选激动剂，但核心是蛋白-蛋白互作与炎症通路，非蛋白质-DNA互作或TF-DNA结合体系，且无AI/物理模拟方法。
abstract: Ischemic stroke is a devastating condition with limited treatment options, where neuroinflammation plays a pivotal role in secondary brain injury. Neural cell adhesion molecule 1 (NCAM1) is implicated in neural development and plasticity, but its specific role in microglia during ischemic stroke remains unclear. Here, we demonstrate that microglial NCAM1 expression is significantly downregulated in the acute phase of ischemic stroke in both human patients and a mouse transient middle cerebral artery occlusion (tMCAO) model. Using microglia/macrophage-specific NCAM1-overexpressing CX3CR1Cre/ERT2 mice, we show that NCAM1 overexpression reduces infarct volume, improves neurological deficits, and enhances long-term functional recovery. Mechanistically, NCAM1 directly interacts with the E3 ubiquitin ligase TRIM67 via its cytoplasmic domain. This NCAM1-TRIM67 complex enhances K63-linked ubiquitination while suppressing K48-linked ubiquitination of IkappaBalpha, thereby stabilizing IkappaBalpha protein, preventing NF-kappaB p65 nuclear translocation, and ultimately inhibiting NF-kappaB-driven neuroinflammation and apoptosis. Furthermore, through molecular docking and high-throughput screening, we identified DB07993 as a potent NCAM1 agonist. DB07993 treatment mimicked the neuroprotective effects of NCAM1 overexpression in vitro and in vivo, primarily through activation of the NCAM1-TRIM67-IkappaBalpha axis. Our study unveils a novel regulatory mechanism where microglial NCAM1 serves as a critical brake on post-stroke neuroinflammation and identifies DB07993 as a promising lead compound for developing NCAM1-targeted stroke therapies.
abstract_zh: 缺血性卒中是一种治疗选择有限的破坏性疾病，其中神经炎症在继发性脑损伤中发挥关键作用。神经细胞黏附分子1（NCAM1）参与神经发育和可塑性，但其在缺血性卒中期间小胶质细胞中的具体作用仍不清楚。在此，我们证明在人类患者和小鼠短暂大脑中动脉闭塞（tMCAO）模型中，缺血性卒中急性期小胶质细胞NCAM1表达显著下调。利用小胶质细胞/巨噬细胞特异性过表达NCAM1的CX3CR1Cre/ERT2小鼠，我们显示NCAM1过表达可减少梗死体积、改善神经功能缺损，并增强长期功能恢复。机制上，NCAM1通过其胞质域直接与E3泛素连接酶TRIM67相互作用。该NCAM1-TRIM67复合物增强IkappaBalpha的K63连接泛素化，同时抑制其K48连接泛素化，从而稳定IkappaBalpha蛋白，阻止NF-kappaB p65核转位，最终抑制NF-kappaB驱动的神经炎症和凋亡。此外，通过分子对接和高通量筛选，我们鉴定出DB07993为一种有效的NCAM1激动剂。DB07993处理在体外和体内模拟了NCAM1过表达的神经保护效应，主要通过激活NCAM1-TRIM67-IkappaBalpha轴实现。我们的研究揭示了一种新的调控机制，其中小胶质细胞NCAM1作为卒中后神经炎症的关键制动器，并确定DB07993为开发靶向NCAM1卒中治疗的有前景的先导化合物。
